issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
text: As background, Resurgent likely is not legally supposed to be doing collections in Texas. I was unable to verify that Resurgent has a current XXXX XXXX XXXX or XXXX in Texas with their XXXX provider, XXXX XXXX. Resurgent refuses to provide that information. The number they provided to the Texas Secretary of State does not match the number on the letters sent to me as well as discrepancies in the address, so it's likely the XXXX XXXX is expired. If a XXXX XXXX address and phone number are incorrect on the XXXX website, technically the debt collector is unreachable. While this is state-specific, it shows Resurgents disregard for laws. For background, XXXX XXXX, my loan provider, did not provide to me a notice to cure a default before their securitization loan provider, XXXX, charged off the loan on XX/XX/XXXX. Texas law requires a notice to cure default. I disputed this with XXXX XXXX, who was simply looking to clear their books before their XXXX XXXX XXXX acquisition by XXXXXXXX XXXX due to wrap up Q2 of XXXX. XXXX, which wasn't XXXX XXXX or XXXX XXXX XXXX , supposedly was the entity that charged off the loan, not XXXX XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a scammy looking text from a Resurgent Capital. The text didn't show any information, and looked like a phishing attempt. I did make an account with Resurgent instead of clicking that shady text to see if XXXX XXXX had indeed tried to pawn off this loan on someone else since I told them I was aware of the acquisition and what they were trying to do. In fact, I had already filed a CFPB complaint against XXXX XXXX, and they admitted they provided no notice to cure since I had opted out their harassing phone calls. Opting out of phone calls does not mean they get to violate my rights and circumvent the law. My loan was targeted because of my hardship program during my unemployment, but I would have been more than willing to bring it current since I now have good employment. This was all to make way for the XXXXXXXX XXXX acquisition. Once I had my Resurgent account active, I noticed the account had multiple changes in ownership, which were never relayed to me. Resurgent even went back later and tampered with the original account information to make it look like XXXX XXXX had always been owner. I signed my contract with XXXX XXXX XXXX only, not XXXX XXXX, who is only the Servicer. Resurgent shows on the account that the loan was originally with XXXX XXXX XXXX, was charged off by XXXX ( who is not a lender ), and then sold by XXXX XXXX to Resurgent ( LVNV Funding ) on XX/XX/XXXX. When I asked for the full chain of custody showing the sale from XXXX XXXX XXXX to XXXX and from XXXX to XXXX XXXX, and the master purchase agreement with XXXX ( who is not a licensed lender in Texas and was explained to Resurgent multiple times ), Resurgent refused to provide it. I also disputed the amount since the principal amount never reduced after XX/XX/XXXX with payments made all through XXXX. This should have been a red flag to Resurgent, but I doubt anyone there is paying attention to details like that. Resurgent only wants to provide boilerplate debt verification with no real thought or investigation behind it. I have made multiple online disputes, starting from when I was able to access my online account. Resurgent clearly is uncomfortable with my questions since these XXXX XXXX loans are a large part of their portfolio, so in their last email to me they said they would no longer communicate online and all communication had to be through the U.S. mail. Their last letter claims they didn't have enough information to verify any of the items I disputed. I provided plenty of information, so this is a evasion tactic. I have sent multiple follow-ups online to the XX/XX/XXXX letter that were all ignored. Resurgent needs to return this file to XXXX XXXX or XXXX ( it's unclear who actually sold this and charged it off ). Since these companies violated my rights, never sent me a letter to cure default, and XXXX XXXX just wanted to clean up accounts with hardship payments before their acquisition by XXXXXXXX XXXX, this account should have never been sold. Resurgent should have never bothered to collect on a such a problematic file if they couldn't quickly produce the actual chain of custody since they only have numbers on a spreadsheet, not forward flow agreements or bills of sale. It might even be possible Resurgent shouldn't even be collecting in Texas due to the fact their XXXX XXXX could not be verified as active. Resurgent needs to do a better job of actually responding to requests in the future instead of stonewalling. If they are going to have an online dispute process and someone asks an uncomfortable question about the very file they are trying to collect money on, then suddenly they only want to communicate through the U.S. mail, what good is having anything online?

text: To Whom it May Concern : Please let this letter serve as a formal complaint to Mohela and the Department of Education about an issue I have had with several student loans under one account. We made at least 5 lengthy phone calls with Mohela that did not yield clarity or a resolution. Four loans were issued on my behalf back in XXXX. The Master Promissory Notes included an accurate previous address of XXXX which my family has not lived in since XXXX. Any correspondence would have been forwarded for a year, but my mother received nothing. Correspondence about the loans themselves were sent to the address of my estranged father at XXXX. I am a XXXX and have the exact same name as my father. Because my father and I are estranged, he did not contact me about the correspondence that was mailed to him. Even if I had known about these loans, I would have never changed the address to my fathers address due to the nature of our relationship. Additionally, two of the four loans ( XXXX ) do not appear to have Master Promissory Notes. The phone number and email address listed on the Master Promissory Notes have not been in use for at least 5 years. I believe Mohela searched for me and instead found my fathers information because they excluded the XXXX on my name, then began sending correspondence to him in error. Because both the address on the Master Promissory Notes and the correspondence were mailed to the wrong addresses for years, I had no knowledge the loans even existed and therefore have not been repaying them. I did not learn of this debt until I recently attempted to secure a mortgage to buy my first home. This issue has destroyed my credit. sub_issue: Credit card company isn't resolving a dispute about a purchase on your statement
text: Company : Capital One Product : Credit Card ending in XXXX Issue : Billing Dispute-Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation ; improper denial based on timing Summary of the Problem : I am filing this complaint regarding Capital Ones handling of a billing dispute involving unauthorized charges from a moving company. I paid the merchant a lump sum amount in full via XXXX for the agreed-upon services. The merchant required a second payment method on file, so I provided my Capital One credit card solely for that purposenot for payment. No additional balance was owed. Despite this, multiple charges appeared on my Capital One credit card. The merchant later confirmed to Capital One that I had paid in full via XXXX and refunded several duplicate charges. However, XXXX charges {$570.00} and $ XXXX not refunded. These charges were not authorized beyond the original lumpsum payment. Timeline and Dispute Handling Concerns : * I filed my dispute within 60 days of the statement date. * Capital One acknowledged the dispute and requested documentation. * I uploaded all the requested documents multiple times, including written explanations, XXXX proof of payment, and account statements. * Capital One informed me that I had until XX/XX/year>, to provide documentation, yet repeatedly denied my inquiries by XX/XX/year>, claiming the matter was now outside the allowable timeframe. Each time I submitted documents, the case was closed within minutes, without any substantive review or explanation. The case was repeatedly closed and reopened over several months, especially between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/year>, without a proper review of the materials I submitted. On XX/XX/year>, a supervisor stated that the dispute would no longer be reviewed because it was outside the allowable timeframe, despite my timely compliance with all requests. Why This Appears to Violate the Fair Credit Billing Act : I complied with every deadline provided by Capital One. Any delay occurred due to Capital Ones internal handling of the case, not my actions. The pattern of closing the dispute within minutes of receiving documentation, followed by denial based on timing, raises serious concerns about whether Capital One conducted a reasonable and good-faith investigation as required under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ). The FCBA requires creditors to : Review the consumers evidence, conduct a reasonable investigation, and provide a written explanation of findings. Capital One repeatedly closed the dispute without addressing the evidence I submitted. If Capital One relied solely on merchant statements while disregarding consumersubmitted documentation, this would constitute an unreasonable investigation and a potential violation of federal law. Harm to the Consumer : * I was charged for services that were already paid in full via XXXX. The merchant acknowledged the XXXX payment and refunded some charges, confirming the error. * Capital Ones refusal to review the remaining charges leaves me responsible for unauthorized amounts. * The account was not past due, and I am actively trying to resolve the matter to protect my credit standing. * Capital Ones actions create a risk of improper negative credit reporting and financial harm.

text: I am filing a complaint against AmeriCU Mortgage regarding their refusal to properly review my lossmitigation application and their statement that they will do nothing further for me, despite new and material hardship information. I have a documented medical hardship caused by a workplace exposure on XX/XX/XXXX. Because of this exposurerelated condition, I have been unable to work since XX/XX/XXXX. My physician has confirmed my condition and ongoing treatment. During the same period, I experienced abnormally high electric bills due to what I now believe was a faulty meter or transformer issue with my utility provider. My usage dropped immediately after a meter replacement on XX/XX/XXXX. I am filing a formal complaint with the Minnesota XXXX XXXX XXXX regarding suspected longterm overbilling. These two hardships medical and utilityrelated directly caused my mortgage delinquency. Despite this new information, AmeriCU Mortgage informed me that they will do nothing further regarding my lossmitigation request. They have refused to reconsider my application, refused to review updated hardship documentation, and have not offered any alternative options. This appears to violate federal mortgage servicing rules, including requirements to : Consider new hardship information Provide a complete review of all available lossmitigation options Work with HUDapproved housing counselors Provide a single point of contact Provide a written explanation of denial and appeal rights I am requesting that the CFPB require AmeriCU Mortgage to : Reopen and reconsider my lossmitigation application Review all available options, including payment reduction Work with my HUD housing counselor Provide a written explanation of their decision Pause foreclosure activity during review I am seeking a sustainable payment, ideally around {$2000.00} per month, which reflects my current financial situation. Desired Resolution : A full and fair lossmitigation review, including payment reduction options, and compliance with federal servicing rules.

text: {$760.00} XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX Re : Account Number : * XXXX To Whom It May Concern : This letter serves as formal notice pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, specifically 15 U.S.C. 1692c ( c ), that you are hereby instructed to CEASE AND DESIST from any and all communication with me regarding the above-referenced account. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692c ( c ), once a consumer notifies a debt collector in writing that they refuse to pay a debt or that they wish the debt collector to cease further communication, the debt collector must not communicate further with the consumer except to : Advise that further collection efforts are being terminated ; Notify the consumer that certain specified remedies may be invoked ; or Notify the consumer that the debt collector intends to invoke a specified remedy. You are hereby directed to immediately stop : Telephone calls to my home, cell phone, or place of employment Emails or electronic communications Text messages Letters, except as permitted under the statute Contacting third parties regarding this alleged debt Be advised that any continued contact beyond what is permitted under federal law will be documented as a violation of the FDCPA and may result in a complaint being filed with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the Federal Trade Commission, and/or civil action for statutory damages, attorneys fees, and costs. This notice does not constitute an acknowledgment of the alleged debt, nor does it constitute a refusal to pay. It is simply a demand that you cease communication as provided under federal law. Govern yourselves accordingly. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

sub_issue: Didn't receive enough information to verify debt
text: Transworld Systems Inc. for failing to conduct a lawful investigation and for continuing to furnish inaccurate and unverified information to consumer reporting agencies after receiving notice of dispute. The account being reported by Transworld Systems Inc. relates to an alleged collection account for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in the amount of {$1500.00}. I disputed this account directly with the credit reporting agencies. After receiving notice of my dispute, Transworld Systems Inc. continued furnishing the account as accurate without providing competent documentation supporting the debt. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, once a furnisher receives notice of a dispute from a credit reporting agency, the furnisher is required to conduct a reasonable investigation and report accurate results back to the credit reporting agency. Transworld Systems Inc. failed to : conduct a reasonable investigation after receiving notice of dispute provide documentation supporting the balance claimed verify the date of first delinquency provide proof of contractual liability with the original creditor provide chain of assignment authority demonstrate legal authority to collect the alleged debt ensure maximum possible accuracy before furnishing consumer reporting data Despite these failures, the account continues to be reported as accurate. Additionally,XX/XX/XXXX confirmed that reporting information connected to this account was updated after its investigation while still being marked verified as accurate. Updating reporting data during an investigation confirms the information previously reported was not accurate and indicates the furnisher did not properly verify the account. This conduct constitutes violations of : Fair Credit Reporting Act XXXX ( b ) Fair Credit Reporting Act XXXX ( b ) Fair Credit Reporting Act XXXX Fair Debt Collection Practices Act XXXX Fair Debt Collection Practices Act XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I previously sent written notice of intent to pursue civil litigation if these violations were not corrected. Transworld Systems Inc. has continued furnishing inaccurate and unverified information after receiving notice of dispute. I am requesting that the CFPB require Transworld Systems Inc. to : delete the account from all consumer reporting agencies provide documentation supporting their investigation procedures provide documentation supporting their authority to collect this debt If this matter is not resolved, I intend to pursue civil litigation seeking statutory damages, actual damages, punitive damages, and attorneys fees.
